verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Bounds 1 and 2 are stated verbatim. Bound 1 is `pulseAmplitude c ≤ C*lam^30` = e_b ≤ C_pre λ^30. For bound 2, exp c.pulseStart = X_p and angular …(c.pulseStart, eta) = radialAmplitude(pulseStart)·shape(eta) = e_b f(η) = E(X_p,η), so the quotient is M/(X_p E) = 𝒜_{X_p}(U)/E; Lean bounds its value and its η-derivative separately by C λ^29 over |η| ≤ 1, which is the C¹_η norm up to the factor 2. Bound 3 is not one declaration: the Lean normalizes the axial and angular halves of S(X_p) separately by X_p e_b² (not by f²). Recovery: `prefixEnergy c η = prefixAxialEnergy·η² − prefixAngularEnergy·shape η²` is S(X_p) (the ∫U²dX and ∫(E²/2)dX prefix integrals with the η-shapes factored out); the step `hpre` inside `totalEnergy_normalized` gives λ·S(X_p)/(X_p e_b² f²) = normalizedPrefixAxial·(η(1+η²))² − normalizedPrefixAngular; on |η| ≤ 1 one has |η(1+η²)| ≤ 2 and |d/dη(η²(1+η²)²)| ≤ 16, so value and η-derivative are at most 16·(normalizedPrefixAxial + normalizedPrefixAngular); dividing `normalizedPrefix_bound` by λ turns its right-hand side into prefixBoundConstant·(1 + log(1/λ)). That is the paper's third bound with constant 16·prefixBoundConstant.
